A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FreeInv work, and their text, equations, tables and figures are readable. The supplied v1 ends with references; v2 additionally includes Appendices A–F. No reading gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original image and video reconstruction/editing experiments, ablations and human preferences, including Tables 1–6 and Figure 5.

after.justification: Section 4 retains original empirical results, while Appendices A–D report additional inverse-transformation, NTI-combination, SDXL and human-preference experiments.

M1.justification: The ensemble formulation, one-sample-per-step approximation and matched latent transformations remain unchanged. The inverse transformation of predicted noise moves from v1 Section 3.3 to v2 Appendix A. The additional transformation and integration experiments do not introduce a newly specified inversion algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image reconstruction/editing on PIE and video reconstruction/editing using DAVIS and Internet videos. Additional qualitative examples and human comparisons remain within this coverage. SDXL adds a model configuration, not a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: ReNoise joins the P2P editing comparison. More substantially, v2 Table 1 introduces direct U-Net reconstruction comparisons against NTI, EDICT, DI, VI, ReNoise, BELM and PI, beyond v1's editing comparisons. Appendix D also adds human preferences across alternative inversion methods; v1 only reports preferences with versus without FreeInv.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce an SDXL configuration, inverse-transformation and NTI-combination controls, and a multi-method preference study reporting 130 votes. Existing PIE coverage, image resolution, 120-frame video preparation and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Newly disclosed details of retained experiments do not establish that those experiments changed.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained sampling-count, branch-construction and transformation ablations, v2 adds color jitter and tests three substantive questions: whether inverse noise transformation affects reconstruction versus editing, whether FreeInv complements NTI, and whether its benefits transfer to SDXL (Appendices A–C, Tables 7–9). The earlier FLUX analysis is retained and relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. Newly disclosed survey vote counts describe sample sizes rather than uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive reconstruction comparisons, ReNoise editing scores, FLUX resource costs and appendix results, including NTI+FreeInv PSNR 28.15 and FreeInv preference of 30.0% in Table 10. Patch-shuffle PSNR changes from 27.45 to 27.61, with LPIPS and MSE also revised (v1 Table 5; v2 Table 6). Matched existing editing, FLUX reconstruction, video and original preference results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 explicitly specifies independently sampled initial images from the natural-image distribution and writes the mismatch-error expectation over that distribution. This refines the premises of the unbiasedness argument. The triangle inequality and subsequent Monte Carlo derivation otherwise remain mathematically unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction's contribution summary and conclusion shift toward explicit comparable-or-better image/video reconstruction claims across U-Net and DiT architectures, whereas v1 emphasizes competitive image editing and superior video editing. The abstract, ensemble motivation and central efficiency claim remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly acknowledges that FreeInv can preserve source content too strongly and restrict editability, and that editing quality depends on the selected editing framework. Section 3.3 also adds a rationale for using transformed branches without spatial or semantic correspondence. These are substantive qualifications of otherwise retained interpretations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a direct code-access statement, specifies 25-step FLUX and 12-step VI schedules, and documents the retained survey's 15 images, 165 votes, instructions and interface. Conversely, it removes v1's V100-32GB/A100-80GB hardware specifications and explicit statement that rotation is the default comparison transformation. These are documentation changes, not evidence of reruns.

R1.justification: New citations include ReNoise, SDXL, DiT and rectified-flow architectures, ensemble learning, CLIP, LatentWarp and WAVE. The related-work narrative and positioning against optimization-based and error-compensation inversion methods remain largely intact.

P1.justification: v2 polishes language and front matter, rewrites the contribution summary, conclusion and portions of Section 4 around reconstruction, and moves editing integration into Appendix A. FLUX discussion moves into the main reconstruction comparison. The principal section sequence and most methodological and related-work prose are retained.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to single-column layout. Reconstruction and efficiency comparisons are consolidated, editing-table cost columns move into the reconstruction table, and existing qualitative panels are rearranged. Appendix Tables 7–10 and Figures 8–13 add substantial displays; some examples repeat earlier figures rather than provide new evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 fills an important evidential gap by directly benchmarking reconstruction against competing U-Net inversion methods. Appendices A–C test the editing adaptation, compatibility with NTI and transfer to SDXL; comparative human evaluation and explicit limitations further strengthen and qualify the conclusions. These gains substantially improve support for the paper's central claims, outweighing the loss of hardware documentation while preserving the established editing and video results.
